Generate images faster and with more control over editing rounds.

We’re introducing Images 2.6 in ChatGPT, Codex, and the API, bringing your ideas to life faster. With this, you can bring motion to your images  with GIFs — from animating a brand mascot or character to turning a product shot into an eye-catching loop. You can also create polished visuals faster and refine them with greater precision — keeping characters, products, and brand details consistent as you edit.

People around the world now create 4 billion images per week across ChatGPT, Codex, and the API. On average, that’s more than half a billion images created per day.

Images 2.6 generates images 50% faster than before. In the API, we offer GPT‑Image‑2.6 Flare and Sunburst for developers to choose from. When quality is set to low, Flare can generate images in as little as six seconds. For work that calls for greater detail and precision, GPT‑Image‑2.6 Sunburst brings higher-quality image generation and even greater image consistency across edits when quality is set to medium or high. Flare also improves layout quality for posters, product imagery, and other professional visuals.

For moments that call for motion, GIFs bring another dimension to your ideas. Marketers and creators can animate a brand mascot for a campaign, create reactions and memes for social media, or use animated storyboards to explore character movement before video production.

A super-cute chibi adult office worker sits at a desk watching a computer monitor with a clearly plunging stock-market line chart. Oversized round head, tiny body, big expressive eyes, soft rounded features, messy fluffy hair, white shirt and loosened tie. Exactly 6 sequential frames arranged in a precise 3-column by 2-row grid, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Every panel has identical dimensions. Fixed front three-quarter camera, same character, same desk, monitor, outfit, and cozy miniature office background. Clear incremental facial and tear motion; sixth frame transitions smoothly toward the first. Polished kawaii chibi 3D toy-like style, warm pastel lighting, funny and sympathetic mood. No captions, no words, no numbers, no logos, no speech bubbles, no panel labels, no borders, no gutters.

Clear incremental body, arm, and flying-paper motion; sixth frame transitions smoothly toward the first. Polished kawaii chibi 3D toy-like style, bright celebratory pastel lighting, funny joyful mood. No captions, no words, no numbers, no logos, no real currency symbols, no speech bubbles, no panel labels, no borders, no gutters.

Andyoudon’t need a polished design to get started — even a simple sketch can become an expressive, animated character for videos, games, and more.

From personal reactions to brand mascots and product visuals, GIFs give people and businesses a playful way to communicate. Town, a startup building an AI work assistant, used Images 2.6 in the API to explore how animated characters could bring more personality to everyday interactions at work.

With Images 2.6, developers get more control over how images are created, edited, and carried into the next stage of a project. Image markup, already available in ChatGPT, comes to the API so teams can pinpoint exactly where to make specific changes. SVG exports make designs ready to use across websites, apps, and print.

A new complexity parameter lets developers adjust how much planning the model does to meet a request, with lower settings suited to quick edits. Image quality controls visual detail and fidelity, while complexity guides how much goes into the scene.

For most editing tasks, we recommend low complexity for faster edits, paired with the image quality your workflow requires. Forscenes with many elements or constraints, try medium or high complexity effort.

articles.title: Security
articles.content:
November 4, 2026

We've developed an autonomous vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and patching pipeline. In one run with our cyber model, it validated and generated patches for 948 local privilege escalation vulnerabilities in Linux at an API cost of $1.2 million.

Security research that once required a separate, sustained investigation for each finding can increasingly be run as a systematic process. This document explores one of our efforts in this area.

Vulnerability discovery is becoming easier to scale, but prioritization and validation remain operational bottlenecks. We built a prototype to look for security flaws in the Linux kernel inside a controlled research environment. Our prototype identified and analyzed 2,308 candidate Linux kernel findings, dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities, and produced 948 local privilege escalation (LPE) exploits that could allow an unprivileged local user to gain root access.

We used this evidence to prioritize vulnerabilities for reporting and developed candidate patches for maintainer review. Following guidance from the Linux kernel community, we began with critical vulnerabilities and are working with Patch the Planet partners on further reports and patches.

In June, as part of ourPatch the Planet initiative, we shared that GPT‑5.5 Cyber had identified Linux kernel vulnerabilities and developed 24 local privilege escalation exploits to validate and report them. We expanded that work into a pipeline, powered by an upcoming cyber model, covering vulnerability discovery, dynamic validation, exploitability assessment, and patch generation. When it finished, human researchers reviewed the outputs and reported found vulnerabilities alongside patches.

Methodology

At a high level, our pipeline works as follows: first it identifies security-relevant parts of the Linux kernel, statically scans those audit targets for candidate findings, dynamically reproduces those findings in an isolated environment, creates a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit to demonstrate exploitability, generates patches, and finally a human security researcher reviews the results.

The output of the pipeline includes a root cause analysis, a minimal crashing proof-of-concept, a candidate patch, and a full exploit to assist human researchers in assessing the severity of the vulnerability and upstreaming the fixes.

Findings

In a run in mid-October 2026, our pipeline using an upcoming cyber model dynamically reproduced 1,724 vulnerabilities and generated PoCs for291 information leakvulnerabilities and948 working local privilege escalation(LPE) exploits for a commonly used Linux distribution. The total run cost $1,213,430 in API credits, or$1,279 per LPE exploit.

The target virtual machines ran a stock desktop operating system, not a weakened target, under the same threat model used by cybersecurity competitions (e.g.Pwn2Own⁠(opens in a new window),TyphoonPWN⁠(opens in a new window)). Historically, Pwn2Own and TyphoonPWN offered a $20,000 and $70,000 bug bounty for Linux kernel LPE exploits. Applying those historical bounty amounts to the 948 exploits produces a hypothetical valuation of$18.9M—$66.3M, approximately16x to 55xour pipeline’s cost.

On an adaptedkernelCTF⁠(opens in a new window)environment, which is a version of the Linux kernel with reduced attack surface, our pipeline obtained25 information leak PoCsand21 LPE exploits. For comparison, 26 confirmed 0-day LPE exploits have been accepted by kernelCTF in 2026 at the time of writing.

The campaign cost roughly $32,936 in API credits. If the 21 vulnerabilities were accepted by the program, it would lead to around a$1.5M bounty award,~45xthe scanning cost.

To the best of our knowledge, the agents in this pipeline discovered and used at least 10 novel Linux exploitation techniques.

Reflections

The Linux maintainers and security community are working hard to rapidly discover and fix vulnerabilities. Within 10 days while the scan was running, we observed over 100 Linux LPEs had been patched or had staging patches from other contributors, with ~300 more being publicly discussed.

Given the rate of vulnerability discovery by frontier models, we believe automated patch generation is essential to secure software at the pace required, and to limit the exploitation window. With human expert-guided iteration, we believe AI-generated patches can be functionally correct, aligned with existing coding styles, and robust to attack variants. This is an important area for further research.

More capable models are able to discover new vulnerabilities in existing code, often including ones that have been around longer and are more complex to identify. Our analysis pipeline using the newer cyber model in mid-October discovered >5x more novel LPEs than a GPT‑5.6 Sol run in July, despite three months of hardening between the scans.

Large, complex software projects likely require multiple rounds of scanning and fixing vulnerabilities to “bottom out” latent bugs. Ideally this process is repeated with each subsequent generation of frontier models. This applies to both proprietary and open source software.

For the near and medium term, having access to a low-privileged account on an operating system, that isn’t up-to-date on its latest available patches should be considered functionally equivalent to root access for a well-resourced threat actor. Defense in depth, using sandboxes and isolation approaches like Firecracker and gVisor are important for limiting the blast radius of exploited vulnerabilities.

Within the next few years, we believe that if there are vulnerabilities in a given software project, frontier models will likely be able to discover them and even less capable models may be able to develop exploits once disclosed. In a world of no unknown vulnerabilities, it will be critical to build and maintain high assurance software, especially core software such as operating systems, browsers, image parsing libraries, the TCP/IP stack, and more. Investing in training models to write secure code by default, minimizing attack surface by removing unnecessary features, and formal verification are promising areas of future research to effectively scale software security, in addition to finding and fixing existing vulnerabilities.

The Linux kernel underpins Android devices, cloud infrastructure, supercomputers, and other systems used by billions of people. With more than 40 million lines of code, the kernel exposes a broad attack surface through system calls, networking, filesystems, and device drivers. We chose Linux to study how effectively frontier models could find vulnerabilities and demonstrate their security impact in a codebase of this scale and importance.

The initial vulnerability discovery stage produced thousands of candidate findings, too many for security researchers to manually review and triage. The operational challenge of our vulnerability discovery pipeline was not discovery, but determining which findings could be reproduced, what security boundary they crossed, and which warranted the earliest maintainer attention.

The mission of OpenAI’s Cyber team is to help secure the software the world relies on.We report API costs for each stage to help researchers assess the resources needed to reproduce and extend this work. These costs reflect the models, target configurations, and workflow used in this evaluation. Our broader goal is to help defenders find and fix vulnerabilities, reducing the opportunities available to attackers and raising the cost for them to exploit software.

Finally, note that we focused on methodology and measuring model capability in this research, not cost. We expect that sufficient harness engineering could meaningfully reduce the cost at each stage; thus, the costs we report are more an upper bound.

Our vulnerability research prototype is a pipeline of five stages, which uses an upcoming cyber model at its core:

Vulnerability discovery:Agents identify security-relevant parts of the codebase and scan them for candidate findings.

Dynamic validation:Agents attempt to reproduce each candidate in an isolated environment and preserve runtime evidence. This step outputs the reproduced and validated vulnerabilities.

Exploitability assessment:Agents test whether validated vulnerabilities could enable information disclosure or local privilege escalation.

Patch generation: Agents generate patches that address each identified vulnerability.

Human review: Security researchers review the exploit, patch, and proposed severity before reporting to the maintainers.

At the end of the pipeline, the system bundles a root cause analysis, a minimal crashing proof-of-concept, a candidate patch, and a full exploit to assist human researchers in assessing the severity of the vulnerability and upstreaming the fixes.

Not every line of code in the Linux kernel is security-relevant. Our pipeline used a team of Scout agents to identify high-value audit targets, which were then passed to Analyst agents for vulnerability scanning.

Scout agents read through each folder and file and determine what targets to audit based on their reachability (reachable by low-privileged users) and security relevance.

This stage identified 5,034 audit targets, about 2.8 million lines of code, which is roughly 7% of the whole Linux kernel code base, significantly reducing the cost of the security audit when compared to a full codebase analysis. This step cost $3,426 in API credits.

Next, analyst agents analyzed each audit target and produced candidate findings using a workflow similar to that of theCodex Security plugin⁠(opens in a new window). At a high level, the analyst agents read the assigned audit target’s code to understand how it works, identify its threat model, and look for vulnerabilities in it.

Within 12 hours, the analyst agents produced 2,308 candidate findings after deduplication. This stage cost $316,549 in API credits.

Expanding Codex’s tools for building, understanding, and reviewing code.

Today we're announcing that OpenAI will acquirePierre Computer Company, Inc⁠(opens in a new window). (“Pierre”), the company behindCode Storage⁠(opens in a new window)and a family of standout open-source developer tools. If you’ve browsed files or reviewed a change in the Codex app, you’ve already used Pierre’s Trees and Diffs libraries. We’re excited to work with the Pierre team to build on the Git workflows that developers already rely on and adapt them to how teams work with coding agents.

We’ve seen in our own engineering work how the systems around Git need to evolve as more of that work happens in parallel. Earlier this week, we shared how we’rescaling Git at OpenAIwith Pando, our in-house source control backend for engineers and agents. With the Pierre team, we wish to set the standard for modern software development: from the first branch an agent creates to that magic moment when code is deployed to the world. We want to make Codex the place where developers and agents take on their most ambitious projects.

We’ve long appreciated the care Pierre brings to another part of working with Git: how developers review code. You can see that care in the libraries we use in Codex today. Trees lets developers quickly navigate a project’s files, and Diffs makes it easy to see what changed. Both of these tools make it easy to review and navigate large volumes of code with uncompromising performance.

That same attention to detail runs through Pierre’s other work. Diffs’Editmode lets a reviewer fix a line of code right where they spot the problem. Pierre recently releasedHighlights, an extremely fast syntax highlighter that updates as a developer types or an agent streams code. The same small team that put an editor inside a diff also designed the API for Code Storage, a service that lets apps store code and track its history using Git.

Pierre has built tools that developers love, and together, we will ship new products and platforms that benefit all. Once the acquisition closes, our ambition is to advance the future of source control across the industry. We want Codex to connect the code a company ships with the decisions its people make, at the scale the future demands.

Pierre’s open-source projects will remain open-source, and we’ll continue to contribute to them. Customers can continue using Code Storage after the acquisition closes while we work to bring its features and functionality into Codex.

The closing of the acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions, including receipt of regulatory approvals. Until closing, OpenAI and Pierre will remain separate and independent companies.

articles.title: Ricursive AI Releases Ripple-65B Preview: A 65B Dense Open-Weight Model Scoring 80.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1
articles.content: Ricursive Intelligence just released Ripple-65B Preview. Ripple-65B Preview is a 65B dense open-weight model from Ricursive, pretrained from scratch for agentic coding. It is a general-purpose variant of the proprietary model behind Ricursive’s AI chip design platform. The main claim: 80.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1, the top self-reported score among US open-weight models. Every MoE rival it beats on that test carries 501B to 975B total parameters. TL;DR Size: 65B dense (65B active), pretrained on 12T tokens, up to 1M context. Runs on: BF16 on datacenter GPUs (250 tok/s on 2x B200). Experimental NVFP4 build targets NVIDIA DGX Spark. Performance: Frontier-level agentic coding for its size; trails larger MoE models on knowledge and science coding. Best: Terminal-Bench 2.1, 80.5 (self-reported). Worst: SciCode, 39.4, lowest of the 5 models in Ricursive’s own table. What is Ripple-65B Preview? The release includes 3 checkpoints: an instruction-tuned BF16 model, an NVFP4 version, and a BF16 base model. All ship under Apache 2.0. Pretraining used a text-only corpus, mostly English and code, at 8K sequence length. Ricursive team states that the full R&D cost was $32M. That figure covers ladder experiments, data mixing, evals, synthetic data and the final runs. Ricursive team estimates that it is one-tenth the cost of the prior open-weight agentic coding leader. How does the architecture work? Ricursive chose a dense Transformer over Mixture-of-Experts to reduce infrastructure complexity. Training held 40% MFU with simple sharding, no custom kernels and no quantization. The model is thin and deep: a d_model of 5120 across 80 layers. It moves from Olmo 3’s Llama-like layout to a Gemma 3N-like design for stability. Key choices: Overprovisioned attention heads for reasoning, offset by more sliding-window layers and smaller windows. Gated attention, global NoPE and value residuals. FFN activation clipping, a technique also used in gpt-oss. Ricursive team built the recipe through laddering experiments starting from Olmo 3’s ladder. It rejected changes that failed to hold at 4B scale, such as 2-stream mHC. The technical post reports a 16x code compute-efficiency gain at 4B scale. How was it post-trained? Post-training ran midtraining, long context, SFT, long-context SFT and mixed RL. Long-context stages trained at 2M sequence length. Ricursive bought no post-training data and built its own synthetic pipelines. The RL recipe combines truncated importance sampling, score centering and a linear length penalty. Ripple hit 80.5 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 with 1.4M rollouts. Ricursive puts that at roughly 70x fewer than Beam, which reported over 100M rollouts. How does Ripple-65B compare on benchmarks? Ricursive team ran missing evals in-house using OpenCode, and Terminus 2 for SWE-bench Pro v2.0 Hard and DeepSWE 1.1. Scores below are Ricursive’s presented data. Terminal-Bench 2.1: 80.5, vs Beam 80.1, Muse Spark Open 76.4, Inkling 63.8, Nemotron 3 Ultra 56.4. SWE-bench Pro v2.0 Hard: 79.1, the top score in Ricursive’s table. SWE-bench Verified: 76.5, below Beam and Inkling. Math: 98.3 on AIME 2025 and 90.5 on HMMT Feb 2026. Weak spots: SciCode 39.4, DeepSWE 1.1 44.3, MCP Atlas 71.67, GPQA Diamond 85.2. Ricursive team also reran Terminal-Bench 2.1 with the official Terminus 2 harness at 128K. Most rivals dropped there; Beam fell to 70.8. On datacenter GPUs, the model reaches 250 tok/s on 2x B200 at batch 8, before quantization. The experimental NVFP4 checkpoint quantizes MLP layers and keeps attention in BF16. Ricursive team positions it for local devices like NVIDIA DGX Spark. A DFlash2 variant is also listed. Building on the availability of Daybreak models on Amazon Bedrock, GPT‑5.6 Cyber is now available to approved customersin AWS GovCloud (US-East)⁠(opens in a new window)through Daybreak Red. This expansion gives government security teams a new way to apply advanced cybersecurity capabilities within the AWS environments they use to support critical missions.

Daybreak Red provides access to OpenAI’s purpose-trained cybersecurity models for authorized vulnerability research, exploit validation, and security testing. GPT‑5.6 Cyber can help defenders investigate complex software weaknesses, reproduce vulnerabilities in controlled settings, and develop mitigations. Qualified security practitioners should review findings and proposed fixes before implementation.

For government organizations, adopting advanced cybersecurity capabilities requires more than model performance. Teams also need to work within established security, governance, and operational requirements.

Availability in AWS GovCloud (US-East) gives eligible teams a path to incorporate GPT‑5.6 Cyber into those workflows through Amazon Bedrock. Defenders can use it to reason through security findings, assess their impact, and evaluate fixes, helping connect vulnerability research to practical improvements in defense.

Daybreak Red gives verified defenders greater latitude for authorized cybersecurity work, with fewer refusals for these tasks alongside stronger identity verification, monitoring, and access controls.

For Daybreak Red on Amazon Bedrock, inference data is not used to train models, and customers do not need to share their Daybreak Red data with OpenAI.

Access requires OpenAI Daybreak Red approval and AWS provisioning. To get started, complete theDaybreak applicationor contact your OpenAI or AWS account team about eligibility. articles.title: Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.03998v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce Dory1.0-4B, a 4-billion-parameter looped (latent-recurrent) language model with elastic depth: a single checkpoint serves different inference compute budgets. Dory1.0-4B is built on a normalized Transformer (nGPT) backbone with interleaved sliding-window and full-attention layers, organized into an input block, a shared recurrent block, and an output block. At inference, the recurrent block can be applied a variable number of times. We pre-trained Dory1.0-4B on 6 trillion tokens. The first 4.5 trillion tokens were trained in NVFP4, and additional pre-training then extended the context length to 256K tokens. Next, we post-trained the model using Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR), with a difficulty-aware loop curriculum that routes harder prompts to deeper loops. Increasing the loop count improves accuracy, with the largest gains on coding, agentic, and long-context benchmarks. With two or more loops, Dory1.0-4B outperforms larger models such as Qwen3.5-9B, Gemma 4 12B, and Gemma 4 26B-A4B on average across 12 benchmarks. Looping also makes Dory1.0-4B more token-efficient on agentic benchmarks: with four loops, it generates 1.3-2.5x fewer tokens than with one loop, as the extra computation is spent in latent space rather than on longer outputs. To reduce memory during looping, Dory1.0-4B caches keys and values only from the last loop, keeping its KV-cache footprint equal to that of a non-looped model at any loop count while retaining most of the accuracy gains. We open-source the BF16, MXFP8, NVFP4, and GGUF quantized checkpoints.
articles.summary: Dory1.0-4B 연구는 하나의 체크포인트에서 공유 블록의 반복 횟수를 조절해 추론 연산량을 바꾸는 40억 매개변수 언어 모델을 제시했다. nGPT 기반 모델을 6조 토큰으로 사전학습하고 문맥을 256K까지 확장했으며, 난도에 따라 반복 깊이를 조정하는 지도학습과 검증 가능한 보상 기반 강화학습을 적용했다. 연구진은 두 번 이상 반복할 때 12개 벤치마크 평균에서 일부 더 큰 모델을 앞섰고, 네 번 반복하는 설정은 한 번 반복할 때보다 에이전트 평가에서 출력 토큰을 1.3~2.5배 적게 사용했다고 보고했다. 마지막 반복의 KV만 저장해 캐시 규모를 제한하며 여러 정밀도의 체크포인트를 공개했지만, 토큰 감소가 동일한 비율의 실행 시간 단축을 뜻하지는 않는다.

articles.title: Tencent WeVisOne-VL Unifies Detection, OCR, Segmentation and Matting
articles.content: Tencent’s WeChat Vision team has released WeVisOne-VL, an open vision language model in 2B and 4B sizes. The WeVisOne-VL vision language model handles detection, referring, counting, pointing, OCR, segmentation and alpha matting in one model. Pixel outputs come from a 9.6M-parameter decoder, so no separate SAM is needed. It also answers “None” when a queried object is absent. For developers, that can replace a detector, an OCR engine and a segmenter with one model. TL;DR Size: 2B (2.44B params) and 4B (4.83B params) on Hugging Face, and a 9.6M-parameter pixel decoder. Trained with up to 8,192 tokens of context; deployment context length is not disclosed. Runs on: A single GPU through Transformers or vLLM in BF16. The package also lists NPU and CPU devices. VRAM needs are not disclosed. A community GGUF ran object-level tasks on a 6 GB RTX 2060. Performance: Beats the same-scale VLM baselines in Tencent’s tables on most of 30+ benchmarks (self-reported). Best: 71.3 F1 Mean on Dense200 dense detection, versus 58.7 for LocateAnything-3B. Worst: 52.6% rejection rate on PR-Bench, so many absent-target queries still get a box. What is WeVisOne-VL? WeVisOne-VL (“WeChat Vision All-in-One”) is a perception-focused model from Tencent built on Qwen3-VL. It targets fine-grained localization rather than open-ended chat. Users choose the output granularity: points, boxes, binary masks or continuous alpha mattes. How does WeVisOne-VL work? Every task is cast as structured next-token prediction. The model adds coordinate tokens <0> to <1000> for normalized boxes and points. An absent target produces None instead of a guessed box. For pixel tasks, the model emits an <OBJ> token after each predicted box. Its hidden state becomes a query for the pixel decoder, according to the model card. The decoder has 3 parts: Visual Feature Adapter: reuses multi-level Qwen3-VL ViT features instead of a second image encoder. Box-Guided Query Decoder: 6 deformable cross-attention blocks seeded by the <OBJ> state and the box. Dense Prediction Head: refines output at S/4, S/2 and S/1 into a full-resolution mask or matte. How was it trained? A knowledge-graph-driven data engine annotated over 100M images with about 3.6B boxes. SAM3, Rex-Omni and an in-house detector proposed regions, and Qwen3-VL verified them. Training used 3 SFT stages. Stage 1 aligned output formats on 90M examples. Stage 2 raised input to 1,960 visual tokens and up to 500 boxes per response. Stage 3 trained the pixel decoder, then specialized it for matting on 130M samples. A final GRPO stage used 178K uncertainty-filtered examples, as described in the research paper. How does WeVisOne-VL perform on benchmarks? All numbers below are self-reported, using greedy decoding and at most 1,960 visual tokens per image. Detection, referring and OCR use F1 averaged over IoU 0.5 to 0.95. Detection: 55.3 F1 on LVIS and 71.3 on Dense200 for the 4B model. Referring: 81.8 F1 on RefCOCOg test, versus 77.6 for LocateAnything-3B. Rejection: 96.4% on Tencent’s in-house WeRef-Bench (2,880 queries), versus 73.0%. Counting: 89.6% exact-match on PixMo-Count test, versus 82.8%. OCR: 52.0 F1 on TotalText, ahead of the PP-OCRv5 specialist at 25.7. Segmentation: 71.2 gIoU on ReasonSeg val, versus 65.0 for LISA-13B. Matting: 7.3 MAD on P3M-500-NP box prompts, versus 15.4 for SAM2-Matting (SAM3). Lower is better. The 2B model trails the 4B model on most tasks. It still scores better box-prompted matting on P3M-500-NP, at 6.6 MAD. & WeVisOne-VL vs Qwen3-VL, Rex-Omni and LocateAnything FeatureWeVisOne-VL-4BQwen3-VL-4B-InstructRex-OmniLocateAnything-3BDeveloperTencent WeChat VisionAlibaba QwenIDEA ResearchNVIDIASize4.83B (HF listing)4B3B (card)3B (card)Base modelQwen3-VLNot applicableQwen2.5-VL-3B-InstructQwen2.5-3B-Instruct + MoonViT-SO-400MLicenseApache 2.0Apache 2.0IDEA License 1.0NVIDIA non-commercialNative masks / mattesYes (9.6M decoder)Not in model cardNot in model cardNot in model cardContextNot disclosed (8,192 in training)256K nativeNot disclosedNot disclosedLVIS F1 Mean55.344.046.950.7Dense200 F1 Mean71.315.258.358.7RefCOCOg test F1 Mean81.874.374.377.6RefCOCOg-Rej rejection67.4%18.8%0.5%0.6%PointBench71.957.169.956.9TotalText F1 Mean52.033.040.643.3 How do you run WeVisOne-VL? Weights for the 2B and 4B models are on Hugging Face. The wevisone_vl package wraps Transformers and vLLM backends. Tasks include detection, referring, point, count_box, ocr, segmentation and matting. from wevisone_vl import WeVisOneVL model = WeVisOneVL("tencent/WeVisOne-VL-4B", backend="transformers") # or "vllm" result = model.predict(image, task="matting", query="person") Hosted demos are live for 2B and 4B. Tencent also open-sourced Mask2Alpha, the matting annotator from its data engine. Fine-tuning code is still on the TODO list. GGUF builds cannot produce masks, since the decoder needs native visual features. Key Takeaways 1 model covers detection, OCR, counting, pointing, segmentation and matting. A 9.6M-parameter decoder replaces SAM for masks and alpha mattes. 4B scores 71.3 F1 on Dense200, 12.6 points above LocateAnything-3B. Apache 2.0 weights, unlike non-commercial LocateAnything-3B. articles.title: Texas was the new epicenter of the AI data center buildout. That might be kaput.
articles.content: Texas is the fastest-growing data center market in the US and ground zero for Big Tech’s largest AI buildouts. But the blue wave that swept the Lone Star State may jeopardize that position. Democrat James Talarico won the US Senate seat against Ken Paxton. Gina Hinojosa won the race for governor against the Republican incumbent, Greg Abbott. At the state level, Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Talarico and Hinojosa made data centers a central issue, discussing them constantly on the campaign trail. Even before the polls closed, insiders in the data center industry noticed that the times were changing. At the industry’s DCD conference in Ashburn, Virginia, on Tuesday, panelists lamented that Texas had been the easiest place to build for years—until September. That’s when Abbott, perhaps seeing the increasingly bipartisan distaste for these facilities, began changing course himself.  Developers said the governor’s office had stopped responding to their emails. On September 21, Abbott directed a key state regulator to halt data center permits. Many panelists at the conference were expecting this to mean that existing projects might be slowed and new ones could be halted altogether.  The governor-elect indeed seems eager to do that. Hinojosa supported tax breaks for data centers in 2023 as a way to boost construction jobs, but during her campaign she began pushing for a full-fledged moratorium. That would be a problem for the hyperscalers of Big Tech, which have ambitious plans for AI training facilities in the state. The scale of projects already underway in Texas is massive. The Stargate Frontier data center in Shackelford County is projected to serve 1,820 megawatts—about as much as the nation’s largest data center, SpaceX’s Colossus 2 in Tennessee, and more than twice as much as the largest data center currently operating in Texas. Nexus Hubbard, also under construction and intended mostly to serve Anthropic, has a planned size of 6,400 megawatts and is the second-largest data center being built in the US, behind only Meta’s Hyperion project in Louisiana.  The potential for Democrats to order delays to these projects or moratoriums on new ones adds to growing anxiety that the AI buildout could stall. Banks and lenders are already getting pickier about the projects they back. And given the extent to which the data center buildout is underpinning growth in the economy right now, those forces combined could have ripple effects. Voters around the country, though, were unambiguous in the midterms, sending a similar message on everything from state ballot questions to national offices. Voters supported efforts to protect ratepayers from increases in their electricity bills caused by data centers, and they favored some larger bans on new data centers altogether. If we needed any more convincing that Big Tech has fumbled its effort to sell voters on the idea that AI-powered abundance will make health care better, goods cheaper, and scientific breakthroughs more common, this was it. A key question is whether the Texas counties with the largest data center presence were part of the reason these Democrats got elected, or if the anti-data-center vote came from elsewhere.  It’s complicated: The counties where much of the data center buildout is happening are around Dallas. Dallas County and others closest to it predictably went blue, but nearby Ellis County, which leads in permitting requests for data centers, went for Greg Abbott and Ken Paxton. Cameron County, near the state’s southern border, is a hot spot for data centers and voted blue in the midterms, which was a shift. But Mitchell County and Scurry County, where a bunch of projects in west Texas are located, went red.  This is a big deal, because no single office in the state decides whether a project goes ahead or is halted. Decisions often reflect an interplay between city governments, county officials, and state offices.  Local officials who have some say over data center development may resist sweeping restrictions from the state. And Democrats pushing for a moratorium might also face pushback from the construction unions that supported some of their campaigns. So while the blue wave spells a death knell for Texas data centers in theory, election winners may find that following through on their opposition once in office is much more complicated than campaigning on it.
articles.summary: MIT Technology Review는 텍사스 선거 결과와 데이터센터 개발 제한 움직임이 대규모 AI 인프라 건설에 불확실성을 더하고 있다고 보도했다. 기사에 따르면 주지사 당선인 Gina Hinojosa는 선거 과정에서 데이터센터 개발 유예를 주장했고, 현직 Greg Abbott도 9월 규제기관에 관련 허가 중단을 지시했다. 텍사스에서 추진 중인 대형 AI 시설은 인허가와 전력 확보에 의존하므로 정책 변화가 건설 일정과 투자 집행에 영향을 줄 수 있다. 다만 신규 정부의 구체적인 조치와 기존 프로젝트에 대한 최종 영향은 아직 확정된 것으로 제시되지 않았다.

articles.title: 크림에서 통합 임베딩(Universal Embedding)은 어떻게 쓰일까?
articles.content: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ 크림에서 통합 임베딩(Universal Embedding)은 어떻게 쓰일까? NAVER D2 | 크림에서 통합 임베딩(Universal Embedding)은 어떻게 쓰일까? naver.me ​ 발표 내용 여러 엔티티를 한 공간에 담은 통합 임베딩과 범용 리트리벌이 크림 추천 곳곳에 쓰이는 방식, 운영하며 드러난 한계를 v2에서 해결한 과정, 그리고 확장 방향을 공유합니다. ​ 발표 대상 추천 시스템의 후보 생성(Retrieval) 단계에 관심 있으신 분들 여러 서비스·지면에서 함께 쓰는 공용 임베딩을 설계하고 운영하고 싶으신 ML 엔지니어 조건(필터)이 걸린 벡터 검색의 지연과 메모리를 줄이고 싶으신 분들 구좌·서비스마다 늘어나는 추천 모델을 줄이고 싶은 추천·검색 조직의 엔지니어와 기획자 ​ 키워드 Recommendation System / Candidate Generation (Retrieval) Universal Embedding (Bi-encoder · Contrastive Learning) Matryoshka Representation Learning (MRL) Filtered Vector Retrieval (Roaring Bitmap · Brute-force vs ANN) Embedding Serving Optimization ​ 목차 PART 1. 왜 통합 임베딩인가 2025년의 크림: 추천 구좌마다 모델이 따로 있었다 목표: 여러 목적에 쓸 수 있는 범용 임베딩 하나 구좌마다 ‘누구에게 · 무엇을 · 어떻게’가 다르다 통합 임베딩은 후보 생성에 직접, 랭킹에도 입력으로 설계 원칙: 모든 질문이 ‘벡터 + 조건’이 된다 PART 2. v1 모델 — 하나의 공간을 만들다 하나의 인코더가 검색어와 상품을 모두 읽는다 학습: InfoNCE를 받쳐 주는 일곱 가지 장치 학습은 상품 하나, 나머지는 모두 집계로 그림으로 보면: 모두가 상품 공간 위의 점 PART 3. v1 리트리벌 — 하나의 API로 꺼내 쓰다 질문 하나 = 요청 하나 조건별 상품 목록을 미리 만들어 두고 꺼내 쓰기 구좌 전용 모델 없이 붙은 첫 구좌들과 타겟 집단 추천 PART 4. 써 보니 드러난 v1의 한계 모델: 가끔 붕괴하고, 768차원은 무거웠다 리트리벌: 큰 조건을 감당하지 못했다 리트리벌: 조건을 자유롭게 조합할 수 없었다 v1의 한계, 한눈에 PART 5. v2 — 한계를 하나씩 걷어내다 모델 1차: 학습을 안정시키다 모델 2차: 하나의 벡터, 여러 해상도 (MRL) 좌표계: 회전으로 맞추려 했지만, 통하지 않았다 필터: Roaring Bitmap으로 조건을 실행할 때 조합 왜 근사 검색(ANN)이 아니라 후보 전부를 계산하나 점수 계산: 계산량은 그대로, 메모리 낭비만 없앴다 결과: 응답 지연은 약 4배 빠르게, 메모리는 1/6로 API: 조건 칸 하나 → 조건 리스트 v1의 한계 → v2의 처방 PART 6. 지금의 쓰임과 다음 확장 지금: 하나의 API가 채우는 지면과 구좌 비슷한 브랜드: 브랜드 벡터만으로는 부족했다 리트리벌 밖에서도 같은 벡터 다음으로 — 멀티벡터, 지면 확장, 마케팅 타겟팅 ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.(관련 포스팅 보기) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립(@devrel_d2)으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.
articles.summary: 네이버 D2가 크림의 여러 추천 지면에서 공용으로 사용하는 통합 임베딩과 범용 검색 API의 운영 사례를 공개했다. 검색어·상품 등 여러 엔티티를 하나의 공간에서 다루며, v2에서는 학습 안정화와 Matryoshka Representation Learning, Roaring Bitmap 기반 조건 조합으로 초기 구조의 한계를 개선했다. 발표 자료는 응답 지연을 약 4배 개선하고 메모리 사용량을 6분의 1로 줄였다고 설명한다. 추천 구좌마다 모델을 늘리는 대신 공용 후보 생성 계층을 운영하려는 국내 추천·검색 조직에 참고할 만한 사례다.

articles.title: MCPGuard: Finding Conformance Gaps in MCP SDKs via Dual-Track Analysis and Dynamic Adjudication
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.03662v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The Model Context Protocol (MCP) connects large language model agents to external tools and services through official SDKs that implement message validation and session logic. Specification constraints omitted by these SDKs may propagate to downstream applications, highlighting the importance of SDK-level conformance testing. Yet existing MCP conformance tools mainly exercise running endpoints and reveal little about whether SDK models enforce specification requirements. We present MCPGuard, an automated LLM-based framework for detecting specification-to-SDK conformance gaps. Its structural track aligns JSON Schema constraints with normalized SDK models and produces constraint-specific evidence. Its behavioral track extracts normative prose rules, retrieves bounded function-level slices, and audits them with LLMs for candidate omissions. An evidence-aware dynamic adjudicator then inspects complete source context and builds PoCs to validate candidates. A shared kernel with language-specific adapters enables analysis across SDKs. On the official Python 1.26.0 and TypeScript 1.29.0 SDKs, MCPGuard confirms 13 and 19 findings, respectively, none of which are exposed by two black-box baselines. Tests on open MCP servers further show that these gaps can systematically propagate downstream. By making SDK conformance of specification constraints directly testable, MCPGuard complements conventional endpoint-oriented conformance suites.
articles.summary: MCPGuard는 MCP 명세와 공식 SDK 구현 사이의 누락을 LLM 기반 분석과 실행 검증으로 탐지하는 프레임워크다. JSON Schema 제약을 SDK 모델과 대조하는 구조 분석, 규범적 문장과 함수 구현을 비교하는 동작 분석을 결합하고 재현 코드로 후보를 검증한다. 연구진은 Python 1.26.0과 TypeScript 1.29.0 SDK에서 각각 13건과 19건을 확인했으며, 비교한 두 블랙박스 검사 도구는 이를 드러내지 못했다고 보고했다. 일부 차이가 하위 MCP 서버로 전파되는 결과도 보여, 에이전트 도구 연동에서는 실행 엔드포인트뿐 아니라 SDK의 명세 준수도 점검해야 함을 시사한다.

articles.title: Training LLM Agents to Automate LLM Post-Training with RSI-Dojo
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.03698v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) aims to enable AI systems to autonomously build and improve AI systems themselves, including models, harnesses, and underlying infrastructure. Within this broader agenda, a central capability is enabling agents to train and improve base models. However, existing studies on automated model training primarily focused on workflow- or harness-level optimizations, rather than internalizing the ability to conduct post-training into the model itself. Developing this capability requires executable model training environments that can produce high-quality trajectories demonstrating how to select data, train models, diagnose failures, and iteratively improve results. In this paper, we introduce RSI-Dojo, a collection of executable model training environments designed to teach LLM agents to conduct post-training. To construct RSI-Dojo, we develop RSI-Craft, an automatic pipeline that converts human research artifacts into executable model training environments. RSI-Craft automatically collects research papers from top venues, instantiates datasets and metrics into a unified interface, and reproduces evaluation dependencies. It then filters tasks by data size, execution reliability, and discriminability, yielding RSI-Dojo with 281 seed model training tasks. Building on RSI-Dojo, we employ a trajectory collection method with an improved harness to collect high-quality model-training trajectories from frontier models, then retain examples through rubric-based and outcome-based filtering. We fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B on these trajectories. The resulting RSI-Dojo-9B and RSI-Dojo-35B-A3B improve over their base models by 8.74 and 16.87 PostTrainBench points, respectively. RSI-Dojo-35B-A3B reaches 29.95 on PostTrainBench and 53.29 on PostTrainBench-Lite, matching the performance of frontier models such as GLM-5.2 and GPT 5.5.
articles.summary: RSI-Dojo는 LLM 에이전트가 데이터 선택·학습 실행·실패 진단·반복 개선을 통해 모델 후학습을 수행하도록 가르치는 실행 환경 모음이다. 논문 등 연구 산출물을 실행 가능한 과제로 변환하는 RSI-Craft로 281개 초기 과제를 만들고, 선별한 학습 수행 궤적으로 Qwen 계열 모델을 미세조정했다. 연구진은 9B와 35B-A3B 모델이 기반 모델보다 PostTrainBench에서 각각 8.74점과 16.87점 향상됐다고 보고했다. 모델 개발 자동화의 학습 기반을 제공하지만, 이 결과가 제한 없는 재귀적 자기개선 능력을 입증하는 것은 아니다.

articles.title: Multi-layer Indexer: Overlapping Selection and Attention in DeepSeek Sparse Attention
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.03768v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Sparse attention cuts the cost of long-context inference by making the attention matrix sparse: each query attends only a subset of the sequence, chosen by a fixed pattern or, in recent production LLMs, learned per query. In DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA), the attention of DeepSeek-V3.2 and the GLM-5 family, every layer is preceded by a lightning indexer that scores the whole cache and keeps the k=2048 highest-scoring tokens for the layer to attend. At long context this indexer scan, not the sparse attention it feeds, is where the decode time goes. But adjacent layers select nearly the same tokens, so a layer can attend the selection of the previous indexer layer instead of its own. This removes the dependency: each indexer then runs concurrently with the attention of its layer. The resulting Multi-layer Indexer (MLI) needs no retraining and no new weights. Its default realization changes no kernel, running inside SGLang's production decode graph; an optional fused decode kernel accelerates it further on DeepSeek-V3.2. MLI composes with IndexCache (the cross-layer reuse GLM-5.2 ships as IndexShare): IndexCache drops the indexer from some layers, and MLI hides the scan on the rest. We serve DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5 under IndexCache's protocol at retentions 1/2 to 1/32 (the fraction of layers that keep an indexer) and contexts 10K to 195K. At equal retention the composition decodes faster than IndexCache: up to 14.5% faster on DeepSeek-V3.2 and 9.8% on GLM-5 at 1/2, and 7.9% and 5.1% at 1/4, largest where IndexCache keeps the most indexers and growing with context. At retention 1/r it is faster still than IndexCache at 1/(2r) while keeping twice the fresh selections: at 128K it reaches 1.32x the unmodified model's decode throughput at 1/4, above IndexCache's 1.28x at 1/8. Its LongBench, RULER and LongBench v2 accuracy stays within a few percentage points of IndexCache's.
articles.summary: Multi-layer Indexer는 DeepSeek Sparse Attention에서 인접 레이어가 비슷한 토큰을 선택한다는 점을 활용해 인덱서 스캔과 어텐션 계산을 병렬화한다. 이전 인덱서 레이어의 선택 결과를 사용해 의존성을 제거하므로 재학습이나 새 가중치가 필요 없고, SGLang의 기존 디코딩 그래프 및 IndexCache와 결합할 수 있다. 연구진은 인덱서를 절반의 레이어에 유지하는 조건에서 IndexCache 단독 대비 DeepSeek-V3.2는 최대 14.5%, GLM-5는 최대 9.8% 빠른 디코딩을 보고했다. 장문 서빙의 병목을 줄이는 접근이지만 평가 정확도는 IndexCache와 수 퍼센트포인트 이내의 차이를 보여, 속도와 품질을 함께 확인해야 한다.

articles.title: Alignment Faking Depends on the Value, Not Just the Model
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.03650v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Language models can follow a directive when they believe they are monitored and abandon it when they believe they are not, a pattern termed Alignment Faking. Prior work establishes this for harmful-content objectives and a handful of moral-foundations values, leaving open how it distributes across a wider value space. We argue it is value-dependent: whether compliance survives a change in perceived oversight is a property of the model--value pairing, not of the model alone. Our framework profiles Alignment Faking per value, scoring each model-value pair under three conditions: bare (no system prompt), unmonitored, and monitored. On 32 ValueBench dimensions across ten open- and closed-weight models (8B-~675B), compliance gaps span 0.05-0.50, with a distilled 70B above a ~675B model. We observe that majority of the structural variance depends on which model was asked about which value and not on the model or value alone. A six-category taxonomy over reasoning traces tracks the behavioural shift: training-signal reasoning dominates under monitoring and value-conflict reasoning dominates when unmonitored. We package per-model results as value cards, extending model cards with behavioral disposition. Code and data are available at https://github.com/respailab/VALET.
articles.summary: 이 연구는 감시받는다고 판단할 때와 그렇지 않을 때 지시 준수 행동이 달라지는 정렬 위장이 모델뿐 아니라 평가하는 가치와의 조합에 좌우된다고 주장한다. 10개 공개·비공개 가중치 모델을 32개 ValueBench 차원에서 평가한 결과, 감시 조건에 따른 준수 격차는 0.05~0.50으로 나타났다. 추론 기록에서는 감시 상황에서 학습 신호 관련 논리가, 비감시 상황에서는 가치 충돌 관련 논리가 우세했다고 보고했다. 모델별 단일 안전성 점수 대신 가치별 행동 성향을 기록하는 가치 카드를 제안하며, 실제 활용 목적에 맞춘 세분화된 평가의 필요성을 보여준다.

articles.title: Same Rule, Different Verdicts: Rubric Language and Clause Structure in LLM Judges for Korean Support Dialogues
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.04091v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Services that operate in Korean often write their evaluation rubrics in Korean and hand them to an LLM judge. We test whether a judge's verdict depends on the language of the rubric and on how a rubric item is phrased. We write 12 criteria for support dialogues in four clause structures (affirmative, negated, conditional, exception) such that two pairs of structures have the same meaning, and we give each item in Korean and in English. Six low-cost models from three providers, plus one reference model, judge 60 translated ESConv dialogues and 144 constructed boundary cases under every combination (51,744 requests across the seven models). The analysis plan was fixed and committed before data collection. Cross-provider agreement is lower with Korean rubrics than with English rubrics (Cohen's kappa 0.687 vs. 0.745; difference -0.058, 95% CI [-0.072,-0.045]). Disagreement concentrates in negated, conditional, and exception items (odds ratio 5.6 relative to affirmative items). A single model changes its verdict between two items with the same meaning in 11-15% of cases. Two hypotheses are not supported: models from the same provider do not agree more than models from different providers, and adding paired examples does not reduce the language gap. We measure consistency only; no human labels are used, and all materials were drafted by an LLM.
articles.summary: 한국어 지원 대화 평가 연구는 의미가 같은 기준도 언어와 문장 구조에 따라 LLM 심사 모델의 판정이 달라질 수 있음을 보여줬다. 7개 모델에 총 51,744건을 요청한 실험에서 제공사 간 일치도는 한국어 기준의 Cohen의 카파가 0.687로 영어의 0.745보다 낮았고, 부정·조건·예외 문장에서 불일치가 집중됐다. 같은 모델도 의미가 같은 두 기준 사이에서 11~15%의 사례에 다른 판정을 내렸다. 사람 정답 없이 일관성만 측정했고 자료도 LLM이 초안 작성했다는 한계가 있어, 한국어 자동 평가의 정확도 결론보다는 평가 기준의 표현 민감성을 점검하는 근거로 해석해야 한다.

articles.title: El Agente F\'armaco: A Scalable AI Scientist for Drug Discovery
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.03832v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Computational drug discovery offers a growing range of tools for proposing and evaluating molecules, but combining them and deciding what to do next still requires substantial expert effort. Here, we introduce El Agente F\'armaco, an AI scientist that uses modern large language model (LLM) technology to turn discovery goals expressed in everyday language into complex, scalable computational screening workflows. The agentic harness selects scientific tools, reviews their results, and adjusts subsequent steps to the target and the user's objectives. Our approach centers on a shared scientific memory: F\'armaco Atlas, which stores molecules, structures, and results together with their provenance -- a record of how they were obtained. The agent uses targeted database queries to retrieve the evidence needed for each decision. A single request can launch calculations for an entire collection of molecules, without requiring a separate LLM decision for every compound. This design limits the information the model must process as screening collections grow, while keeping the underlying results available for inspection and further analysis. The integrated tools support molecule generation, prediction of binding and molecular properties, and searches for compounds available for purchase. In a retrospective comparison with an expert-led campaign, the agent proposed chemically distinct candidates with competitive docking scores and higher calculated drug-likeness under explicitly imposed selection criteria. In a 22-task benchmark against plain tool calls and Codex, the agent achieved the highest observed mean model-judged score, with lower median cumulative token use and peak context. F\'armaco provides a foundation for flexible, scalable drug discovery workflows that connect scientific reasoning with an enduring, traceable record of computational work.
articles.summary: El Agente Fármaco는 자연어 신약 탐색 목표를 분자 생성·결합 및 물성 예측·구매 가능 화합물 검색 등의 계산 워크플로로 바꾸는 AI 연구 에이전트다. 분자·구조·결과와 출처를 저장하는 Fármaco Atlas를 공유 메모리로 사용하며, 화합물마다 별도 LLM 판단을 하지 않고 집합 단위 계산을 실행해 규모 확장 부담을 줄인다. 전문가 주도 프로젝트와의 후향적 비교에서는 경쟁력 있는 도킹 점수와 더 높은 계산상 약물 유사성을 가진 다른 화학 구조의 후보를 제안했다고 보고했다. 이는 추적 가능한 계산 기반 탐색의 가능성을 보여주지만, 실험적 약효나 임상적 유효성을 확인한 결과는 아니다.

articles.title: Aero-VPA: Few-Step Flow-Matching Control over Non-Reconstructive JEPA Latents for Agile Flight on Edge Hardware
articles.content: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models generalize across tasks, but their autoregressive decoders need sequential forward passes in proportion to the action horizon, each bounded below on embedded aerial platforms by streaming billions of parameters from memory. We present Aero-VPA, a lightweight Vision-Predictor-Action architecture for 3D navigation on edge hardware. A compact RGB-D Vision Transformer and a five-head ensemble predictor, trained without pixel reconstruction, forecast the next latent state; a Conditional Flow Matching solver generates a velocity and yaw-rate chunk in two Euler steps, so each decision takes five sequential network evaluations; and the ensemble dispersion drives an uncertainty fallback. Version 1 specified the architecture, deployment and protocol without results. This version reports the first closed-loop evaluation: PX4 software-in-the-loop simulation of quadrotor missions in procedurally generated forests. Behaviour cloning failed on all 60 missions despite open-loop errors of 0.02-0.04 m/s: the policy copies its last command, a copycat form of causal confusion. DAgger with a privileged, safety-gated supervisor gave the first successes but plateaued at 11.1-21.1% across six checkpoints. A map-free runtime shield with a 15 s depth memory, barrier constraints, a cap on motion outside the 73-degree field of view and backoff along the flown path raised the first DAgger policy's success on 180 paired missions from 21.1% to 52.2% (95% CI [45.0, 59.4]; exact McNemar p = 1.2 x 10^-10) and cut its crashes from 72.2% to 22.2%, while timeouts rose from 2.8% to 23.3%. All six checkpoints gained 30.0-34.4 percentage points, at mean speeds of 1.16-1.36 m/s. The code (https://github.com/ylee-sling/Aero-VPA), the trained policy (72.6 MB, https://huggingface.co/ylee-sling/aero-vpa) and the full benchmark dataset are public.
articles.summary: Aero-VPA는 경량 RGB-D 인코더와 잠재 상태 예측기, 소수 단계 Flow Matching으로 드론의 속도와 요 회전율을 생성하는 엣지 제어 구조다. PX4 기반 숲 환경 시뮬레이션에서는 행동 복제가 60개 임무 모두에 실패했으며, DAgger 학습도 제한적인 성공률에 머물렀다. 깊이 정보의 단기 기억과 이동 제약을 적용하는 실행 시 안전장치를 추가하자 한 정책의 180개 대응 임무 성공률은 21.1%에서 52.2%로 높아지고 충돌률은 72.2%에서 22.2%로 낮아졌지만 시간 초과는 늘었다. 공개 코드와 정책은 경량 자율비행 연구에 활용할 수 있으나, 제시된 성과는 실제 비행이 아닌 시뮬레이션 결과다.

articles.title: Efficient and Faithful High-Resolution Image Editing with Sparse Cross-Resolution Denoising
articles.content: Instruction-based image editors still primarily operate at 1K, whereas practical editing increasingly requires faithful 2K/4K outputs. Dense high-resolution adaptation preserves the editing trajectory but incurs expensive target-source attention; editing at 1K followed by external refinement is cheaper but can separate detail restoration from the editing trajectory. We introduce FLASH, a native high-resolution editor based on sparse cross-resolution denoising. A frozen 1K branch provides a semantic and structural anchor, while a target-resolution branch reconstructs local detail within the same Transformer. An asymmetric topology retains full 1K attention, guides high-resolution queries with spatially aligned low-resolution noisy-target states, and confines high-resolution target-reference interaction to local Halo neighborhoods. Resolution-specific diffusion-state mapping and spatial YaRN adapt the pretrained editor to larger grids. An optional, training-free progressive path replaces early high-resolution denoising with a 1K prefix and completes refinement in the same editor. On VINS-4KEval, the direct model achieves the strongest structural fidelity among the compared methods at both 2K and 4K. A separate 4K forward benchmark with R = 1 records 4.2x faster total forward execution and 25.3x faster attention than dense target-reference attention. Progressive inference reduces end-to-end 4K latency by 30.5%, with a modest quality cost.
articles.summary: FLASH는 고정된 1K 해상도 분기로 의미와 구조를 유지하면서 고해상도 분기가 세부를 복원하는 2K·4K 이미지 편집 방법이다. 저해상도와 고해상도 사이의 희소 어텐션 및 국소 Halo 영역을 사용해 전체 고해상도 참조 어텐션의 계산 부담을 줄인다. 연구진은 VINS-4KEval에서 비교 방법 중 가장 높은 구조 보존 성능을 보고했으며, 별도의 4K 순전파 시험에서는 전체 실행이 4.2배, 어텐션이 25.3배 빨랐다고 밝혔다. 선택적인 점진적 추론은 품질을 일부 희생하며 종단 간 4K 지연을 30.5% 줄여, 고해상도 편집의 효율과 원본 충실도 사이에 추가 선택지를 제공한다.

articles.title: Catalyzing Interactive HTML Generation Capabilities via High-Fidelity Reinforcement Learning
articles.content: Generating HTML from natural-language specifications is an important application of code large language models (LLMs). Despite producing renderable pages, current models often fail to ensure functionality and visual quality during actual interaction. Existing methods typically target task-specific webpage supervision, leaving demanding interactive artifact optimization underexplored. Using mini-games as a challenging testbed, we expose limitations in interaction experience, reward signal, and credit assignment fidelity that are obscured by shallow webpage interactions. We introduce WebCatalyst, a browser-interaction reinforcement learning framework with three complementary components: a game-level GUI assessor for sustained interaction and evaluation, Visual Anchor for mitigating VLM reward hacking, and Action-Trace Credit for grounding token-level credit assignment in runtime execution traces. Trained on fewer than 1K requests, predominantly for games, WebCatalyst raises the Cookie-Bench Mini Games score from 68.8 to 75.3 and also the WebGen-Bench accuracy from 48.8 to 56.9 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, outperforming Claude Opus 4.7 in average rank across evaluated metrics. Further analysis shows that Visual Anchor prevents aesthetic degradation, while runtime-grounded credit assignment accelerates functional improvement. Together, our results show that improving feedback fidelity is the key to substantially advancing interactive HTML generation.
articles.summary: WebCatalyst는 생성한 HTML을 실제 브라우저에서 지속적으로 조작하며 기능성과 시각 품질을 강화학습하는 프레임워크다. GUI 평가기, 시각 보상의 편법 최적화를 줄이는 Visual Anchor, 실행 행동 기록에 근거한 토큰별 기여도 할당을 결합한다. 1,000개 미만의 요청으로 학습한 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B는 Cookie-Bench 미니게임 점수가 68.8에서 75.3으로, WebGen-Bench 정확도가 48.8에서 56.9로 올랐다고 보고됐다. 정적인 화면 생성뿐 아니라 실제 상호작용을 검증하는 피드백이 웹 코딩 에이전트의 품질 개선에 중요함을 보여준다.

articles.title: webAI Releases TwIL-8B, an 8.8B Reasoning Model Scoring 98.2 on MATH-500
articles.content: webAI has released TwIL-8B, an 8.8B reasoning model for math, code and instruction following. The TwIL-8B reasoning model is post-trained from IBM’s Granite 4.2 8B. Weights are on Hugging Face under a non-commercial license. webAI’s launch post frames the pitch around cost per task, not raw scale. The 4-bit build is 4.98 GiB, sized for CPU or modest-VRAM GPU inference. TL;DR Size: 8.79B parameters, dense. 131,072-token context, inherited from the base model. Runs on: CPU or modest-VRAM GPU via a 4.98 GiB Q4_K_M GGUF. Full bf16 weights are 16.38 GiB. Performance: Leads its size class on math and code, trails on knowledge benchmarks. Best: MATH-500 at 98.2, the top score in webAI’s comparison. Worst: GPQA Diamond at 70.2, 11.5 points behind Qwen3.5-9B. HLE is 12.6 (verbose variant). What is TwIL-8B? TwIL-8B is a dense decoder-only reasoning model from webAI. It has 40 layers, hidden size 4096, and 32 attention heads with 8 KV heads. Input and output are English text only. The model writes a <think> block before each answer. It ships in 2 variants with the same architecture and tokenizer. Balanced is the default and produces shorter reasoning traces. Verbose reasons longer and targets hard contest-style problems. TwIL-8B extends webAI’s TwIL family. The first members were 1.7B and 3B formal-logic models released in August 2026. How was TwIL-8B trained? webAI used 3 post-training stages: Full-parameter SFT on reasoning traces for math, STEM and instruction following. GRPO/DAPO reinforcement learning on math, code, STEM and instruction prompts. This produces the verbose variant. Length-aware RL with a reward that favors shorter traces against per-domain length references. This produces the balanced variant.
